name: Rare Earths / Critical Minerals
as_of: 2026-06-09 (scores from stable attributes; tap ↻ for live price/AUM/returns)
tagline: The materials behind magnets, EVs, robotics, wind and defense — where China controls most of the supply. A geopolitical/supply-shock bet with a tiny fund universe and extreme concentration: a textbook binary theme.
universe_note: A VERY thin universe — REMX is essentially the only established fund; CRIT and broad metals-miners (XME/PICK) are the alternatives. Extreme single-name + single-country (China) concentration. Market figures need a live ↻.
key_tensions: China dominance: China controls ~60-70% of rare-earth mining and ~85%+ of processing — export policy there can move the whole theme overnight.
Extreme concentration: REMX leans on MP Materials, Lynas and a few Chinese producers — top-10 dominates; a single name/policy headline swings it.
Tiny universe: essentially one real fund (REMX). Scarcity itself is the finding — and a closure/liquidity concern.
Commodity boom-bust: rare-earth prices are violently cyclical; the equities are higher-beta still.
Strategic tailwind vs price reality: Western governments subsidize supply (defense/EV), but oversupply from China can crush prices regardless.
benchmark_note: XME (SPDR Metals & Mining) or PICK (broad global miners) are the yardsticks — diversified mining vs a narrow, China-exposed rare-earth bet.

memo.thesis: REMX is the one established way to own the rare-earth & strategic-metals supply chain — the magnets/materials behind EVs, robotics, wind and defense. The bet is really a geopolitical one: China dominates supply, and the fund is heavily concentrated in a handful of producers (MP Materials, Lynas) plus Chinese names. Big strategic tailwind, but extreme concentration and commodity-price volatility.
memo.strategy: Passively tracks the MVIS Global Rare Earth/Strategic Metals Index — ~30 companies mining/refining rare earths and strategic metals (incl. lithium, tungsten, titanium). Cap-influenced, so top producers dominate.

purity_verdict.note: Genuine rare-earth/strategic-metals pure-play, though 'strategic metals' broadens it beyond pure rare earths (lithium etc.).
